solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flashy performer who's dressed up with hat

indicators.note: dressed up suggests the letters of who's are disguised in a new arrangement

parts.note: the four letters of who's, taken as written
a boater is a flat-topped straw hat

explanation.surface: A flamboyant entertainer has put on a costume including a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' looks like part of the costume picture, but it signals rearranging the letters of who's; a boater is a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows off to impress an audience is a flashy performer, a near synonym.

clue.text: Southern prophet gets a snack from India

parts.note: Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet from the south is offered an Indian snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried triangular pastry with a savoury filling is a popular Indian snack.

clue.text: More than likely lad goes after rum

indicators.note: goes after places the lad's word behind the rum word in the answer

parts.note: rum in its British sense of strange means odd
a lad is a boy, a son

explanation.surface: A young man follows a glass of rum, and that is probably going to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the drink here but the old British adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting slang: when the odds favour something, it is more than likely to happen.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer to miss trade in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in puts the missing and trading words inside the drink

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink
to lack something is to miss it
the market is trade in general

explanation.surface: A shady trader fails to sell any alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dealing in illicit goods outside legal channels is a dodgy dealer.

clue.text: A jolly fuss about sick creature from South America

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

indicators.note: about means the fuss word goes round the sick word

parts.note: ado is fuss
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A cheerful commotion surrounds an ailing South American animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured burrowing mammal is native to South and Central America.

clue.text: Best selection of Chinese literature

indicators.note: selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Picking the finest works of Chinese writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the pick of the crop.

clue.text: Old group making comeback is just the same

indicators.text: making comeback is just the same
indicators.note: the band's name read backwards, making a comeback, is unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A veteran pop band reforms and sounds exactly as it did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' teases a reunion tour; here it means reading the name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish pop quartet of the 1970s is an old group in the music sense.

clue.text: Handcuff gives couple obstruction

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds
a let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Restraining a prisoner gets two people in each other's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets is slang for handcuffs, so one cuff is a bracelet.

clue.text: One acted in reconstruction as description of incident

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds the letters of one acted in a new order

explanation.surface: A witness performs in a police reconstruction to describe what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short account of a particular incident.

clue.text: Worked out great tactic per training session for the Gunners

indicators.note: worked out means the letters of great tactic per are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A football coach devises a clever plan in training for Arsenal, nicknamed the Gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal football club, but here it means people firing guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting at a mark to improve aim is a training session for gunners.

clue.text: Note money given backing television etc.

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: backing turns the money word backwards

parts.note: aid is money given to help

explanation.surface: A banknote is handed over to fund a TV station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the money word around; 'Note' is a sol-fa syllable, not a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: Television, radio and the press together are the media.

clue.text: Did needlework before wedding announced in London suburb

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken and heard

parts.note: a bride's needlework before the ceremony: made a veil

explanation.surface: A bride sewed before her wedding, which was announced in a London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a veil' said aloud gives the London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Maida Vale is a residential district in north-west London.

clue.text: Hair gets Miliband taken aback

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair
Ed Miliband is a British Labour politician

explanation.surface: A politician's hairstyle has people startled.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband was leader of the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shocked is to be startled, taken aback.

clue.text: Great brain — mine familiarly enjoyed acquiring bit of erudition

parts.note: egg is old service slang for a mine or bomb

indicators.note: acquiring means the enjoyed word takes in the piece of erudition

parts.note: had means enjoyed, as in had a good time

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of erudition

explanation.surface: An intellectual says his own mind took pleasure in gaining a little learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' is not the possessive but an explosive, informally called an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an intellectual, a person with a great brain.

clue.text: Doctor here treats the poorly not the poor!

definitions.text: Doctor here treats the poorly not the poor!

parts.words: Doctor here treats the poorly not the poor!
parts.note: a London street famous for expensive private medical consultants who treat sick but wealthy patients

explanation.surface: A doctor works with the ill rather than the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: The street is in London, home of private specialist clinics.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is famous for private doctors, so medicine there serves the rich.

clue.text: One lonely goatherd's first and last quirky singing style

indicators.note: quirky says the letters gathered are put together in an odd order

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
taken as written

indicators.note: first and last takes the two outside letters of goatherd's

explanation.surface: A solitary goatherd sings in an odd style, recalling the Sound of Music song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' gives G and D; with I and LONELY, 'quirky' rearranges ILONELYGD. The Lonely Goatherd is a song from The Sound of Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is an Alpine singing style alternating chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Cut into hill having got away without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the getaway word around the letter

parts.note: escaped means having got away
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fugitive tunnelled into a hillside and escaped without being stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that is escarped has been cut steep, as a scarp in a hill.

clue.text: Ideas from music shows with piano not right

indicators.note: with brings in the piano letter in place of another
not right removes the right letter as piano replaces it

parts.note: concerts are music shows
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Concepts arise from musical performances that leave out a proper piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In CONCERTS, the R is replaced by P.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept is an abstract notion, an idea.

clue.text: Investors told shockers fraudulently

indicators.note: fraudulently suggests the letters of told shockers are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: Shareholders were told shocking news through fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Holders of company stock are investors in it.

clue.text: Two TVs a source of much entertainment

parts.note: the box is a nickname for a television
a set is a television set

explanation.surface: Having a pair of televisions gives plenty to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxed series of episodes provides many hours of viewing entertainment.

clue.text: Nuisance left quarter pounder

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance
E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An annoying person leaves a quarter-pound burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter pounder' suggests a burger; split them: 'quarter' gives E and 'pounder' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is a tool for pounding in a mortar.

clue.text: Name Child Support Agency for backing hermit

indicators.note: for backing means the name word and agency letters are both read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name, as a reference
CSA is the abbreviation of the former UK Child Support Agency

explanation.surface: A recluse names a government welfare agency as his backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses CITE plus CSA, giving the answer. The CSA was a UK body collecting child maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic renounces comforts, like a hermit living in solitude.

clue.text: Caught yob a hard blow

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lout is a yob, a boorish young man

explanation.surface: A thug was arrested after striking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow with the hand.

clue.text: Put work in to get beating sugar

indicators.note: put tells the solver to place the work word somewhere
in says where it goes: inside the beating word

parts.note: to lose is to get a beating in a contest
an act is a piece of work or deed

explanation.surface: Working hard to beat sugar into a mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is the sugar found in milk.

clue.text: Liven up former Argentine leader with a bit of Italian pizza topping

parts.note: to pep up is to liven up
Juan Peron was president of Argentina

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: Brightening up a former Argentine president with a slice of Italian topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage commonly sliced onto pizza.

clue.text: Trendy group's small figure

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd has a small figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'group's' stands for 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set into a larger one.

clue.text: Character in Morse makes mild expletive

definitions.meaning: the long signal in Morse code, as opposed to the dot
an exclamation of mild annoyance, a euphemism for damn

explanation.surface: A Morse code symbol works as a polite curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the long Morse signal and a gentle oath like 'drat' share this four-letter word.

clue.text: Insect in certain level of development eating vegetable line

indicators.note: eating means the development word swallows the vegetable and line letters

parts.note: a stage is a certain level of development
beet is a root vegetable

explanation.surface: An insect at a particular growth stage is munching a row of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beetle with antler-like jaws, so named after the male deer.
